name: Trackr
description: Portfolios, projects, epics and tasks, kept in one SQLite file on this computer, with tools for Claude Code sessions.

agent.instructions: Work tracking on this computer: portfolios > projects > epics > tasks, with IDs like TC-123. When the user names an ID, call get first: it has the spec, the acceptance criteria and where the last session stopped. Its References are the designs, docs, artifacts and files the work follows, each with a use line: read the ones whose use fits what you are about to do, with the tool for their kind. When work comes from a design or doc, add it to the references of the task, epic, project or portfolio it governs, with a use line, rather than copying it into the description; set key when everything under that should see it. If a change makes a referenced doc wrong, update the doc or say so in the handoff. When you start a task, set it In progress. Before you stop working on it, update it: check the criteria you met, write the handoff (done, left, next) and add a log line. find with no arguments lists open work in this folder's project, next first. Put a whole plan in one create. There is no delete: set an item to Cancelled.

find.description: Lists items one line each, next up first: ID, status, priority, title, epic, criteria done, what it waits on, the session on it. With no arguments: open items in the project of this session's folder. Filters combine.

project.description: A project name, or KEY/Name when the name is in more than one portfolio.

portfolio.description: A portfolio key, like TC: every project in it.

status.description: A status name or a list of them. "open" (the default) is every not-started or active status; "any" is everything.

text.description: Words in the title or description, or an ID.

ready.description: Only items nothing unfinished holds up.

limit.description: At most this many lines. Default 25.

get.description: Everything about one or more items: status, project and folder, session, dependencies, links, description, references (its own, then the key ones of its epic, project and portfolio), acceptance criteria (numbered), where it stands (done, left, next) and the latest log lines. An epic also lists its tasks by project. A portfolio key or project name gives its projects or folders, its open work and its references.

ids.description: IDs like "TC-123", portfolio keys like "TC", or project names like "Desktop" or "TC/Desktop".

log.description: How many log lines, latest last. Default 10.

create.description: Creates portfolios, projects, epics and tasks in one call and replies with their keys and IDs. Portfolios are made first, then projects, then epics and tasks, so an item can name a project made in the same call. A portfolio (kind portfolio: key, name, description) starts with the default statuses and priorities. A project (kind project: portfolio, name, colour, folders) goes in the portfolio whose key it names; a session started in one of its folders lands in it. Epics and tasks can name each other by a temporary ref before they have IDs: epic and waitsOn take a ref or an ID. project defaults to the epic's, then to this session's folder's project. status and priority default to the portfolio's defaults.

ref.description: A temporary name other items in this call use.

project.description: Epics and tasks: a project name, or KEY/Name.

waitsOn.description: Refs or IDs this item waits on.

links.description: "branch feat/x", "PR #412", "commit b7f02c1", "file src/a.py", or a URL: what the work produced. What it follows goes in references.

target.description: A claude.ai artifact's address, a doc or web address, or a file: absolute, ~/..., or relative to this session's folder.

title.description: What it is, like "Sync design". Default: the target.

use.description: When to read it, like "Read when changing the sync engine". Agents decide from this line alone whether to open it.

kind.description: Default: from the target. A claude.ai artifact is artifact; Notion, Google Docs and the like are doc; other web addresses url; anything else file.

key.description: Show it on everything under its owner too: a portfolio's on its projects, epics and tasks. Default false.

references.description: All four kinds: what the work follows, like designs, mockups, specs and docs, each with a line saying when to read it. Reference them rather than copying them into the description.

key.description: Portfolios: what IDs start with, a letter then up to nine letters or digits, like TC.

portfolio.description: Projects: the key of the portfolio it goes in.

colour.description: Projects. Default: the first one the portfolio does not use.

folders.description: Projects: absolute paths, ~/..., or paths relative to this session's folder. A folder belongs to one project only.

update.description: Changes several items in one call: fields, acceptance criteria, the handoff, a log line, links, references and dependencies. Portfolios and projects take only references. Criteria numbers are as get shows them. Replies one line per item, then what became ready. Setting a task to an active status records this session on it.

id.description: An item ID, a portfolio key, or a project name (KEY/Name when it is in more than one portfolio). Portfolios and projects take only references.

epic.description: An epic ID, or null to take it out of its epic.

handoff.description: Where it stands, replacing the last one.

ref.description: What it is about: a commit, a PR.

links.description: What the work produced, as create takes them. What it follows goes in references.

target.description: A claude.ai artifact's address, a doc or web address, or a file: absolute, ~/..., or relative to this session's folder.

title.description: What it is, like "Sync design". Default: the target.

use.description: When to read it, like "Read when changing the sync engine". Agents decide from this line alone whether to open it.

kind.description: Default: from the target. A claude.ai artifact is artifact; Notion, Google Docs and the like are doc; other web addresses url; anything else file.

key.description: Show it on everything under its owner too: a portfolio's on its projects, epics and tasks. Default false.

add.description: As create takes them; a new one needs use. Adding one that is there changes only the fields given.

target.description: A claude.ai artifact's address, a doc or web address, or a file: absolute, ~/..., or relative to this session's folder.

title.description: What it is, like "Sync design". Default: the target.

use.description: When to read it, like "Read when changing the sync engine". Agents decide from this line alone whether to open it.

kind.description: Default: from the target. A claude.ai artifact is artifact; Notion, Google Docs and the like are doc; other web addresses url; anything else file.

set.description: The title, use or key of a reference found by its target; kind only picks between two with the same target.

kind.description: Default: from the target. A claude.ai artifact is artifact; Notion, Google Docs and the like are doc; other web addresses url; anything else file.

references.description: What the work follows: designs, mockups, specs and docs, each with a line saying when to read it.
